Likelihood profiles of a gcTMB model

Source: R/profile.R
profile.gcTMB.Rd

Profiles the (marginal) log-likelihood for single parameters by fixing the parameter at a sequence of values and re-optimising all other parameters, using tmbprofile. With random effects, the profiled likelihood is the Laplace approximation of the marginal likelihood.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'gcTMB'
profile(
  fitted,
  parm = NULL,
  level = 0.99,
  trace = FALSE,
  progress = interactive(),
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'profile.gcTMB'
confint(object, parm = NULL, level = 0.95, ...)

# S3 method for class 'profile.gcTMB'
plot(x, level = 0.95, ...)

Arguments

fitted

A gcTMB object, the result of gcTMB.

parm

Character or integer vector, or NULL. Parameters to profile, names or positions in coef(fitted). Default are the estimated coefficients b1-b5, without the variance parameters.

level

Numeric between 0 and 1. The highest confidence level the profiles are computed for: each profile extends until the deviance from the maximum exceeds the cutoff (see Details). For confint and plot, the confidence level of the intervals and of the cutoff line.

trace

Logical. Print the progress of tmbprofile

progress

Logical. Show a progress bar over the profiled parameters

...

Further arguments passed to tmbprofile, e.g. ystep; ignored by the confint and plot methods

object, x

A profile.gcTMB object, the result of profile.

Value

profile returns a profile.gcTMB object, a list with a data frame for each parameter with the parameter values (par) and the deviance from the maximum (deviance), i.e. twice the difference of the negative log-likelihoods. confint returns a matrix of confidence intervals. plot returns a ggplot object (package ggplot2) with a panel for each parameter, showing the deviance, the cutoff for level (dashed), and the estimate (dotted).

Details

The profiles are computed on the scale of coef: log standard deviations of the random effects (log_sd), parameters of their correlation matrix (corr_par), and the log residual standard deviation (log_sigma), log precision (log_phi), or log size (log_theta) or dispersion (log_phi) of the negative binomial families. The confint method transforms the intervals of the log standard deviations and log precision to the natural scale; correlation parameters are only transformed for terms with two random effects, as their parameter determines the correlation only then. If the profile of a log standard deviation does not reach the cutoff at low values, the likelihood is flat towards zero and the lower limit of the standard deviation is 0. Bounds given by lower and upper in gcTMB are used for the profiled coefficient, but not when re-optimising the other coefficients.

The cutoff of the deviance is the quantile of the chi-square distribution with one degree of freedom. For gaussian and lognormal models without random effects and small-sample inference (see gcTMB), the cutoff of the coefficients b1-b5 is F-based instead, sum(w) log(1 + F/(n - p)) with the quantile F of the F distribution with 1 and n - p degrees of freedom, which gives the intervals of a t-test of each coefficient, as profile intervals of nls.

Examples

fit <- gcTMB(height ~ DAS, data=FabaHeights25)
pr <- profile(fit, progress=FALSE)
confint(pr)
#>                    2.5 %    97.5 %
#> b1:(Intercept) 114.54544 129.48091
#> b2:(Intercept)  29.43847  32.18230
#> b3:(Intercept)  11.21241  15.18937
plot(pr)
